sections.h2: What the Eaton County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
Eaton County's register keeps the county's land title file: deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and any other paper that touches real estate between Charlotte, Grand Ledge, Eaton Rapids and the townships around them. Each filing is checked against Michigan's recording rules and then stored as a digital image.

Counter staff won't draft a deed, and they can't advise you on what a deed should say. Whoever prepared the paper answers for what it says and why, and legal advice has to come from a lawyer. Need a deed written? Hire a title company or real estate attorney, then bring the signed original here.

Weekday counter hours run 8:30 to 4:30, minus a lunch break from noon to 1:00. Courthouse holidays interrupt that schedule, so check the register's page before a holiday week. Anything sent by mail should include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, since the office won't return documents without one.

Most recordings cost a flat $30 apiece, whether the paper is a deed, a mortgage, a lis pendens or a certified real estate copy. The extras are itemized on the county's fees page.

Eaton County register charges
ServiceCharge
Filing one deed, mortgage or similar paper$30
Each further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges$3 each
Tax certificate, first 25 legal descriptions$5
Each description past that$0.20
Ordinary copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2 a page
Certified copy of a recorded document$1 a page plus $5 for the seal

The website does not sell certified copies. Ask at the counter or write to the office.

sections.h2: When does a deed need the treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
Before the register will accept a warranty deed, land contract or land contract assignment, the county treasurer has to certify the parcel. MCL 211.135 sets the test: no tax lien or tax title on the land, and the prior five years of taxes paid.

Exempt from the requirement: quitclaim deeds and similar conveyances lacking warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds, and state tax deeds. The closer normally orders the certificate while escrow is open, so most sellers never request it directly.

What a complete package holds:

  • The treasurer's certificate stapled to a warranty deed or land contract.
  • The full price printed on the deed, or a value affidavit attached.
  • An addressed envelope with postage when the package travels by mail.
  • The $30 filing charge plus $5 for the certificate where one is required.

Filing by mail without a closer? Work through it in this order:

  1. Get the treasurer certificate first if the deed carries warranty language.
  2. Check that the price or value affidavit is on the deed.
  3. Add a check for the $30 charge, plus $5 for the certificate.
  4. Enclose a stamped envelope addressed to yourself.
  5. Send it to the register in Charlotte and watch for the recorded copy.

A package with a missing piece is returned, and the closing can slip a few days. Unpaid taxes on the parcel block a clean certificate until the balance is paid.

Selling a house here brings two transfer charges. The state's share is $3.75 for each $500 of the price (MCL 207.525), and the county's is 55 cents for each $500 (MCL 207.504, the rate for smaller counties). A partial $500 still counts in full.

Both are the grantor's to pay (MCL 207.502 and 207.523), and the treasurer needs the state part within 15 days after delivery of the deed. A contract clause may hand the bill to the buyer, yet by statute the seller carries it.

Seller proceeds shrink by both amounts, so build them into your net estimate. Have the closer print both amounts on the settlement statement ahead of time.

Plenty of deeds owe no transfer tax, provided the document itself names the exemption it relies on. The county exemptions sit in MCL 207.505 and the state ones in MCL 207.526. The two lists agree except for the last family item below.

  • A price under $100.
  • Mortgages and other security instruments, plus their assignments and discharges.
  • Leases and leasehold transfers.
  • Court orders passing title with no price stated.
  • Quitclaim deeds that cure a defect in title the grantee already owns.
  • Land contracts, until legal title changes hands.
  • State tax only: a gift deed running from parent to child or stepchild, or grandparent to grandchild.

Tax paid on a deal that qualified can be recovered under MCL 207.523(4). The seller, or a buyer who paid in the seller's place, applies to the state Department of Treasury.

sections.h2: Searching Eaton County land records online
sections.html:
Before you list, pull your own deed from the online index and read the legal description, so you know the instrument that will be recorded matches what you plan to convey. The search link on the register's page reaches every record from 1836 up to the most recent proof date, which lets you follow the full chain of title without leaving home. A link for electronic filing sits beside it.

With electronic filing, a title company can send the signed deed in on the same day and skip the courier. Ask your closer whether the file goes in that way and when the recorded copy will reach you. Taxes owed on a parcel are a different search, run through the county treasurer.

sections.h2: Eaton County housing and where the courthouse is
sections.html: The county counts 109,581 residents as of July 2025 and 48,090 housing units. Owners live in 74.2% of homes. The median owner-occupied value is $216,900, while the median renter pays $1,092 a month. Charlotte holds the courthouse, and the register's counter is there. Other cities include Eaton Rapids, Grand Ledge, Olivet and Potterville, and part of Lansing lies within the county.

sections.h2: What happens when Eaton County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent bills are the county treasurer's job, and the same office is the foreclosing unit for parcels that stay behind. Its page says over 2,000 foreclosures have been prevented since 2016 and links a chart of Michigan's foreclosure deadlines.

Pay online after looking up the parcel number and amount in the county's tax search. A 2.49% fee applies to cards, and parcels inside Lansing use their own link. A county land bank deals with vacant and foreclosed property.

You can still sell with a balance due. The closer pays it from your proceeds, guided by what the treasurer's certificate says must clear. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer before listing and confirm it again near closing. Cash buyers skip lender appraisal and underwriting, though a warranty deed still needs the certificate before recording.

faqs.q: Where is a deed filed in Eaton County?
faqs.a: Go to the Register of Deeds in Charlotte, the county seat. Find the counter location on the register's page at eatoncounty.org. It is open weekdays 8:30 to 4:30, closed for lunch at noon.

faqs.q: How much does Eaton County charge for a filing?
faqs.a: Each document is $30. When one assignment or discharge covers several instruments, add $3 for each extra one. A tax certificate costs $5 for up to 25 descriptions.

faqs.q: Can an Eaton County deed be filed online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the e-record link on the register's page. Paper filings by mail need a stamped envelope addressed back to the sender.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Eaton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, under state law. The purchase agreement can pass the cost to the buyer. The state share is due within 15 days after delivery.

faqs.q: How old are the records online?
faqs.a: They go back to 1836 and run through the latest proof date. For certified copies, contact the register's office directly.
